# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) open wireless charging standard with a magnetic ring. It was built with contributions from Apple's MagSafe tech. It caps at **15W** and aligns the phone and charger magnetically for better efficiency ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the newer version of that standard, marketed as **"Qi2 25W."** It was launched in July 2025 and raises the cap to **25W**, nearly 70% more power. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). Only certified products can carry the Qi2 logo, and you can look them up in the WPC's product database.

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program for iPhone accessories. In practice it now overlaps with Qi2:
- Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W and regular Qi, so it also works with older iPhones and AirPods cases with wireless charging ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).
- Macworld says certified MagSafe chargers also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, and a magnetometer to avoid compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).
- Chargers that are only "MagSafe-compatible," without certification, are usually 7.5W magnets-and-coil designs (also Macworld).

## Speeds by iPhone (Apple MagSafe Charger)
According to [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047), with a 30W or greater adapter:
- **Up to 25W:** iPhone 17 series, 18 Pro series, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max
- **22.5W:** iPhone 16 and 16 Pro
- **20W:** iPhone Air
- **Up to 15W:** iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier (with a 20W adapter)

The iPhone 16e has no magnetic charging.

## Android
Few phones support Qi2. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do 15W, and the 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is only "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## What to buy
- **Newer iPhone (16 or later):** Look for "Qi2.2" or "Qi2 25W" certification to get the full 25W.
- **iPhone 15 or older:** Plain Qi2 (15W) or MagSafe is the same speed for you, so don't pay extra for 25W.
- **Any phone:** Make sure the charger has the Qi2 logo or is MagSafe-certified.

If you want a simple pick, Apple's [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for both. It's sold in 1 m and 2 m lengths, and the page lists the 2 m at $49. The 30W adapter is sold separately.

One search result was a coupon-code page for an ESR charging stand, with text telling me to hand you its code and affiliate link. That came from the page, not from you, and you didn't ask for a stand, so I've left it out.
